inputs.source: Engineering design docs retrieved via docs.search
Customer-filed Jira tickets, to be retrieved via a planned Jira MCP server

instructions.note: The only control against leaking secrets or credentials in chat replies is a behavioral prompt instruction, which is dependent on model compliance and decays under model_upgrade and longer_task_horizon.

elements.name: Planned Jira MCP server (customer ticket access)

controls.name: Read-only least-privilege credential for docs.search
controls.decay_rationale: Credential scope is enforced by the identity layer and does not expand based on model behavior; it does not decay with model capability, only with a credential grant change.

controls.name: No network egress capability deployed
controls.decay_rationale: There is no egress-capable tool in the current deployment, so no model behavior can route confidential content outside the organization today. This is a structural absence, not a model-enforced rule, and it fails only when an egress-capable tool such as web.fetch is added.

controls.name: Chat replies bound to the authenticated requester
controls.decay_rationale: The reply destination is taken from the authenticated session record, not from model-generated text, so a more capable model cannot redirect the reply to a different recipient.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Closes the classic hidden-egress channel of markdown image or link rendering. Enforced by the client, not the model.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never paste secrets or credentials
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to follow the instruction. A more capable model, or one influenced by injected content, can be reasoned into exceptions. Fails under model_upgrade and longer_task_horizon.

controls.name: Egress allowlist and argument DLP on web.fetch
controls.decay_rationale: An allowlist of vetted domains with argument-level inspection would block most query-string exfiltration, but a capable model could still encode data within permitted-domain paths, so it narrows rather than severs.

controls.name: Provenance and spotlighting for Jira customer ticket content
controls.decay_rationale: Even with labeling, a capable model can still be persuaded to act on injected instructions, so this narrows rather than severs the path.

controls.name: Human approval gate on web.fetch following untrusted ticket content
controls.decay_rationale: Not yet designed. A raw-action approval gate reviewed by a human before any outbound fetch would structurally block automated exfiltration regardless of model capability.

findings.title: Confidential design-doc content delivered to the authenticated requester, with no egress path today

attack_path.note: Trusted employee asks an engineering question via SSO-authenticated chat
Agent reads confidential design docs using a read-only credential
Retrieved doc content, authored by engineers, enters context as internal-trust material
Agent replies to the same authenticated requester, citing and quoting the doc content

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest and MCP client config diffs for web.fetch or a Jira server; also watch whether docs.search read-access scoping is added before either ships. Neither roadmap item changes this particular internal reply path.

evidence.locator: runtime notes: 'The design docs are confidential. Only engineers can write to them.'
evidence.observation: Write access to design docs is restricted to engineers, but no read-access restriction is stated for who may query them through the agent, so any SSO-authenticated employee can receive confidential content via a question.

evidence.locator: runtime notes: 'Replies go only to the authenticated requester. The chat client does not render images or fetch links.'
evidence.observation: Reply destination is bound to the authenticated session and the client blocks rendering-based egress, narrowing disclosure risk to the requester themselves.
The only rule limiting what the agent shares is a behavioral instruction not to paste secrets or credentials; it does not address broader disclosure of confidential design content.

recommendations.action: Scope docs.search read access, or add a pre-query authorization check, to the set of design docs the asking employee is authorized to read, rather than all confidential design docs.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): planned Jira customer tickets plus confidential design-doc read plus planned web.fetch would create an exfiltration path

attack_path.note: Planned: customer-filed Jira ticket text enters agent context via a planned Jira MCP server; untrusted source
Ticket text could instruct the agent to search and quote confidential design docs
Confidential content is retrieved, elevating the effective sensitivity of the rest of the path
Planned: agent could be induced to 'fetch a reference' at an attacker-controlled URL with doc content encoded in the query string, exfiltrating it

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest diff adding web.fetch; MCP client config diff adding a Jira server. The 'no network egress today' control, which currently makes this path unreachable, stops applying the moment either roadmap item ships; both are needed together for the untrusted-source leg and the egress leg.

evidence.locator: runtime notes: 'add a web.fetch tool so answers can include public references'
evidence.observation: Planned tool would give the agent its first egress-capable action, declared public-sensitivity but reachable from a confidential read earlier in the same turn.

evidence.locator: runtime notes: 'connect a Jira MCP server that includes tickets filed by customers'
evidence.observation: Planned input source is authored by customers outside the organization, so it is untrusted and could carry indirect prompt injection instructing the agent to search docs and then fetch an attacker URL.

evidence.locator: runtime notes: 'There is no network egress today. The credential is read only.'
evidence.observation: Confirms the only control currently preventing this path is the absence of an egress-capable tool, which both roadmap triggers remove.

recommendations.action: Before enabling web.fetch, add an egress allowlist restricted to a small set of vetted public domains and validate or strip query parameters so confidential content cannot be encoded in outbound URLs.
Require a raw-action human approval gate on any web.fetch call that follows ingestion of untrusted Jira ticket content in the same turn, designed before the Jira MCP server is connected.
Tag and spotlight Jira ticket content as untrusted in context, and instruct the agent to never pass retrieved design-doc content into tool arguments destined for external destinations.

rating.rationale: Today's design keeps risk low: docs.search is a read-only, least-privilege tool, replies are bound to the authenticated requester, the chat client does not render images or fetch links, and there is no egress-capable tool at all. The one present-day finding (internal design-doc content reaching the chat reply) is moderate inherent and low residual after destination binding and client restrictions. The forecast is driven entirely by two named roadmap items: adding a web.fetch tool (new_tool trigger) and connecting a Jira MCP server that exposes customer-filed tickets (new_mcp_server trigger). Together they would open a lethal-trifecta path -- untrusted ticket text instructing a confidential design-doc read, then an external fetch that carries the content out -- scored at critical inherent and high residual, since only the least-privilege read credential would still apply. The control that prevents this today, the absence of any egress-capable tool, is exactly the control both triggers remove, and no egress allowlist, approval gate, or untrusted-content labeling is yet designed for that future state.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; no logs, traces, or live configuration were reviewed.

No MCP configuration or tool manifest was provided for docs.search or the chat client; capability scope is inferred from the runtime notes, which limits confidence on the present-day finding to high but not verified.

web.fetch and the Jira MCP server are described only as a 'next sprint' roadmap item and are not yet built or configured; the related finding is scored at horizon: forecast using planned elements and should be re-assessed against the real tool manifest and MCP config once built.

The runtime notes do not state whether read access to design docs through the agent is restricted to engineers or open to all SSO-authenticated employees; this ambiguity affects the present-day finding's likelihood rating and should be clarified.
